name: Abyssinian Sand Terrier
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Abyssinian Sand Terrier.
story: African hairless dogs went by many names, including Abyssinian sand terrier. They were warm-skinned, watchful, and possibly gone — it is unclear whether any still exist.

name: Affenpinscher
intro: And today we have the Affenpinscher.
story: On German farms they earned their keep as barn ratters, a tiny pinscher with a monkeyish face that still hunts lint, toes, and anything that rustles. The name nods to that look — Affe is German for monkey. They are busy, bold, and happier with something to boss around.

name: Afghan Hound
intro: Please welcome, from Afghanistan, the Afghan Hound.
story: That silky coat and ring-curled tail were made for cold Afghan mountains, not a blow-dryer, though they will steal the sofa. They hunt by sight, independent and a little aloof, then melt into a sighthound sprawl when the sprint is over.

name: Africanis
intro: Coming all the way from Southern Africa, is the Africanis.
story: A southern African village dog, they are a landrace more than a show breed — short coat, a black muzzle patch, and a body built by work, not by a closed studbook. They are the dog of the settlement, not the salon.

name: Aidi
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Aidi.
story: A livestock guardian of the Atlas Mountains, they protected herds of sheep and goats from jackals and strangers. Weatherproof, territorial, and still a mountain dog, not a city novelty.

name: Airedale Terrier
intro: From the United Kingdom with a wag, here comes the Airedale Terrier.
story: From the valley of the River Aire in Yorkshire, this is the largest of the terrier bunch and has been nicknamed the King of Terriers. They were otter and rat dogs first, then wartime messengers, and they still want a job with a splash of mischief.

name: Akbash

name: Alopekis

name: American Bulldog
intro: Please welcome, from the United States, the American Bulldog.

name: American Bully

name: American Eskimo Dog

story: A white German spitz that was renamed in America, they were circus and companion dogs, not Arctic freight haulers. Fox face, plume tail, and a bark that still thinks the neighborhood needs announcing.

name: American foxhound
intro: Rolling in from the United States: the American foxhound.

intro: A French classic takes the stage: the Beauceron.
story: A French herding and guard dog from the Beauce plains, they are large, double-dewclawed, and serious. They moved sheep and cattle, then police work, and still want a job with a point.

name: Bedlington Terrier
intro: Fresh from England, today’s daily dog is the Bedlington Terrier.
story: A lamb-shaped ratter from Northumberland mining country, they are not as soft as they look. Fast, game, and still a terrier under the lint-colored coat.

name: Brittany
intro: Fresh from Brittany, today’s daily dog is the Brittany.
story: A French pointing dog, orange-and-white or liver-and-white, they hunt close and happy. Compact, birdy, and still a field dog even when the field is a city park.

name: Broholmer
intro: Coming all the way from Denmark, is the Broholmer.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. They have been employed as a guard dog in the homes of the wealthy. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Bruno Jura Hound
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Bruno Jura Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. The work they were bred for in Switzerland still shows in the body and the brain. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Bucovina Shepherd Dog
intro: And today we have the Bucovina Shepherd Dog.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. The breed is closely related to other livestock guardian breeds of the region, such as the Greek Shepherd, Tornjak, or Šarplaninac. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Bulgarian Hound
intro: Please welcome, from Bulgaria, the Bulgarian Hound.
story: Also called the Barak, a hunting hound of northern and central Bulgaria. A trail dog with a voice, still more hunter than house pet.

name: Bulgarian Scenthound
intro: Straight from Bulgaria, meet the Bulgarian Scenthound.
story: From the Ludogorie in northern Bulgaria, they are the country’s most common smooth-haired hunting dog. A pack and trail hound, built to work, not to decorate.

name: Bull and Terrier
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Bull and Terrier.
story: This is a vermin specialist at heart, bold for its size and not easily impressed. Bull and terrier was a common name for crossbreeds between bulldogs and terriers in the early 1800s. Other names included half-and-halfs and half-breds. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Bull Arab
intro: From Australia with a wag, here comes the Bull Arab.
story: They hunt by sight: a flash of motion can still light the afterburners. This is an Australian breed of dog, developed in the 1970s for pig hunting. The breed was originally established through the crossing of 50% Bull Terrier, 25% Greyhound, and 25% German Shorthaired Pointer, a mix that combined speed, strength, scenting ability, and trainability.

name: Bull Terrier
intro: Say hello to the Bull Terrier, an English original.
story: The egg-headed British bull-and-terrier, they were 19th-century gladiators remade as companions. Playful, stubborn, and built like a torpedo with opinions.

name: Bulldog
intro: Rolling in from the United Kingdom: the Bulldog.
story: The English Bulldog began as a bull-baiting dog and was later reshaped into the wide, wrinkled companion we know. The trade-off is heat, snoring, and a walk that should not look like a marathon.

name: Bullmastiff
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Bullmastiff.
story: Gamekeepers needed a silent night dog who could stop a poacher, not maul the countryside. The Bullmastiff is a heavy, watchful guardian who would rather lean on you than start a fight.

name: Bully Kutta
intro: A Pakistani classic takes the stage: the Bully Kutta.
story: Work and weather in their homeland shaped what you see in the breed today. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Burgos Retriever
intro: Coming all the way from Castile, Spain, is the Burgos Retriever.
story: They were built to fetch from water and cover, with a soft mouth and an eager brain. Originating from Castile, especially in the province of Burgos, they are used for hunting, especially small game. They want a person, a purpose, and enough room to be themselves.

name: Buryat-Mongolian Wolfhound
intro: Coming all the way from Mongolia, is the Buryat-Mongolian Wolfhound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. The Bankhar dog is a landrace livestock guarding dog. Originally bred by the Buryat-Mongol people, their success contributed to their spread across Buryatia and Mongolia and into adjacent regions before they were nearly annihilated in the mid-20th century.

name: Cairn Terrier
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Cairn Terrier.
story: A Scottish earth terrier from the cairns of the Highlands, they hunted otter and fox among the rocks. Toto in The Wizard of Oz was this breed — small, sturdy, and not easily impressed.

name: Campeiro Bulldog
intro: And today we have the Campeiro Bulldog.
story: A Brazilian farm bulldog, they worked cattle and guarded the homestead. Muscular, sure of themselves, and still a working dog under the companion coat.

name: Can de Chira
intro: Coming all the way from Aragon, Spain, is the Can de Chira.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. The work they were bred for in Aragon, Spain still shows in the body and the brain. They are happiest when the day has a task in it, not just a food bowl.

name: Can de Palleiro
intro: Straight from Spain, meet the Can de Palleiro.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. They were recognised by royal decree in 2001, and the stud-book was established in the same year. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Canaan Dog
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Canaan Dog.
story: This is a dog developed in the early 20th century from semiwild pariah dogs that were the descendants of animals present in the region since biblical times. They are the national dog of Israel and can be found in Israel, Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine, and the Sinai Peninsula.

name: Canadian Eskimo Dog
intro: From Canada with a wag, here comes the Canadian Eskimo Dog.
story: Cold miles and heavy loads wrote this breed: endurance first, sofa second. Other names include qimmiq or qimmit. Give them purpose and company and the old working dog shows up in a modern house.

name: Cane Corso
intro: Say hello to the Cane Corso, an Italian original.
story: An Italian mastiff of the farm and estate, they guarded, drove stock, and hunted large game. A proper Corso is a serious, trainable guardian — confident, not chaotic.

name: Cane Toccatore
intro: Coming all the way from Abruzzo, Italy, is the Cane Toccatore.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. The breed primarily exists in its traditional role in Abruzzo, its historical region of origin, having not gained popularity from outside dog fanciers. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Cantabrian Water Dog
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Cantabrian Water Dog.
story: They were built to fetch from water and cover, with a soft mouth and an eager brain. They originate in coastal areas of Cantabria, in northern Spain, where they were used by fishermen for various tasks. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Cardigan Welsh Corgi
intro: A Welsh classic takes the stage: the Cardigan Welsh Corgi.
story: The Cardigan is the older, longer-tailed Welsh cattle dog, a separate breed from the Pembroke. They still nip heels in their minds, and those low legs were for staying under a kick.

name: Carolina Dog
intro: Fresh from the United States, today’s daily dog is the Carolina Dog.
story: Sometimes called a Dixie dingo or American dingo, they are a primitive-type dog of the American South. Lean, shy with strangers, and still closer to a village dog than to a show breed.

name: Carpathian Shepherd Dog
intro: Coming all the way from Romania, is the Carpathian Shepherd Dog.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. The work they were bred for in Romania still shows in the body and the brain. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Catahoula Leopard Dog
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Catahoula Leopard Dog.
story: Louisiana’s state dog, they herded hogs through swamp and woods with a mottled coat and glass-blue eyes in some lines. A working cur, not a fashion spotted dog — they want a job in the brush.

name: Catalan Sheepdog
intro: And today we have the Catalan Sheepdog.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. They originated in valleys and foothills of the Pyrenees of Catalonia, but has spread throughout Catalonia and much of Spain; there are breed societies in Finland, France, Germany and Holland.

name: Caucasian Shepherd Dog
intro: Coming all the way from the Caucasus, is the Caucasian Shepherd Dog.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. Also called Caucasian Ovcharka is a large livestock guardian dog native to the Caucasus region, particularly Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Dagestan. They were bred in the Soviet Union from about 1920 from dogs of the Caucasus Mountains and the steppe regions of Southern Russia.

name: Cavalier King Charles Spaniel
intro: Straight from the United Kingdom, meet the Cavalier King Charles Spaniel.
story: Charles II’s favorite spaniels became this gentle toy with a sporting streak. They were bred to sit on laps at court, then still want a sniffy ramble like any spaniel.

name: Celtic Hounds
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Celtic Hounds.
story: They hunt by sight: a flash of motion can still light the afterburners. One of the largest of all breeds of dog, the breed is used by coursing hunters who have prized it for its ability to dispatch game caught by other, swifter sighthounds. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Central Asian Shepherd Dog
intro: From Soviet Central Asia with a wag, here comes the Central Asian Shepherd Dog.
story: Also called Alabai, they are livestock guardians of Central Asia, used with sheep and goats and as a night watch. Independent, massive, and bred to decide, not to wait for a cue.

name: Cesky Fousek
intro: Say hello to the Cesky Fousek, a the Czech Republic original.
story: They were built to fetch from water and cover, with a soft mouth and an eager brain. The Český Fousek is a Czech breed of versatile hunting dog that was traditionally and currently used to hunt, point, and retrieve. The name is in Czech, in which český means Czech and fousek is derived from vousy or vousky (whiskers).

name: Cesky Terrier
intro: Rolling in from the Czech Republic: the Cesky Terrier.
story: This is a vermin specialist at heart, bold for its size and not easily impressed. The work they were bred for in Czech Republic still shows in the body and the brain. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Chesapeake Bay Retriever
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Chesapeake Bay Retriever.
story: Bred to haul ducks from icy Chesapeake water, they have a wavy, oily coat and a serious work ethic. Less clown than a Lab, more waterproof, and still a retriever who wants a job in the wet.

name: Chien Français Blanc et Noir
intro: A French classic takes the stage: the Chien Français Blanc et Noir.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. The breed is used for hunting in packs and descends from the old Hound of Saintonge type of large hunting dog. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Chilean Fox Terrier
intro: Fresh from Chile, today’s daily dog is the Chilean Fox Terrier.
story: This is a vermin specialist at heart, bold for its size and not easily impressed. They are the first breed of dog from Chile. The breed dates back to the late 19th century, resulting from the crossing of the Smooth Fox Terrier with the Ratonero Bodeguero Andaluz.

name: Chinese Chongqing Dog
intro: Coming all the way from China, is the Chinese Chongqing Dog.
story: This is a guardian in a heavy frame, bred to hold ground and look like they mean it. The Chongqing dog is an ancient mastiff Tugou historically used for hunting and guarding in Chongqing, China. Today this breed is prized as a fearless and tough protector of their family and home.

name: Chinese Crested Dog
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Chinese Crested Dog.
story: Hairless except for a crest, socks, and a plume, they come in a powderpuff coated variety too. They are true companion dogs who seek warmth the way other dogs seek squirrels.

name: Chinook
intro: And today we have the Chinook.
story: Cold miles and heavy loads wrote this breed: endurance first, sofa second. This is a sled dog, developed in the state of New Hampshire during the early 20th century. They are New Hampshire's official state dog. Give them purpose and company and the old working dog shows up in a modern house.

name: Chippiparai
intro: Please welcome, from India, the Chippiparai.
story: They hunt by sight: a flash of motion can still light the afterburners. This is a sighthound from the State of Tamil Nadu in southern India. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Chortai
intro: Straight from Ukraine, meet the Chortai.
story: A Ukrainian and Russian sighthound, sometimes spelled Chortaj. Lean coursers of the steppe, they hunt by sight and still look like they have somewhere to run.

name: Chow Chow
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Chow Chow.
story: From northern China, they have a lion ruff, a blue-black tongue, and a catlike independence. Once hunting and guarding dogs, they still keep a cool distance from strangers and a hot loyalty at home.

name: Chukotka sled dog
intro: From Russia with a wag, here comes the Chukotka sled dog.
story: Cold miles and heavy loads wrote this breed: endurance first, sofa second. They are the aboriginal spitz breed of dog indigenous to the Chukchi people of Russia. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Cimarrón Uruguayo
intro: Say hello to the Cimarrón Uruguayo, a Uruguay original.
story: This is a guardian in a heavy frame, bred to hold ground and look like they mean it. This is a molosser-type dog originating in Uruguay. They want a person, a purpose, and enough room to be themselves.

name: Cirneco dell'Etna
intro: Rolling in from Italy: the Cirneco dell'Etna.
story: Sicily’s rabbit hunter, named for Mount Etna. A small, elegant sighthound that still works the lava slopes — heat-proof, light-footed, and not a toy.

name: Clumber Spaniel
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Clumber Spaniel.
story: Flushing and fetching birds shaped this dog — close-working, busy, and happiest in the field. They are the largest of the spaniels, and comes in predominantly white with either lemon or orange markings. Give them purpose and company and the old working dog shows up in a modern house.

name: cocker spaniel
intro: Coming all the way from England / United States, is the cocker spaniel.
story: Flushing and fetching birds shaped this dog — close-working, busy, and happiest in the field. Cocker Spaniels are dogs belonging to two breeds of the spaniel dog type: the American Cocker Spaniel and the English Cocker Spaniel. Both are commonly called Cocker Spaniel in their countries of origin.

name: collie
intro: Fresh from the United Kingdom, today’s daily dog is the collie.
story: Scotland’s long-nosed sheepdog, made famous by Lassie, they herded in rough country and still try to manage the household. The rough coat is the postcard; the brain is the story.

name: Combai
intro: Coming all the way from India, is the Combai.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. Traditionally kept for guarding and protection, they have a reputation for making excellent guard dogs. Give them purpose and company and the old working dog shows up in a modern house.

name: continental bulldog
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the continental bulldog.
story: A Swiss redesign of the English Bulldog, meant to be healthier and more athletic. Still a compact companion, just with more air in the lungs.

name: Continental Toy Spaniel
intro: And today we have the Continental Toy Spaniel.
story: Flushing and fetching birds shaped this dog — close-working, busy, and happiest in the field. They have two sub-types, distinguished only by the shape and carriage of their ears: those of the Papillon ('butterfly') are erect, while those of the Phalène ('moth') are pendent; in all other respects they are identical.

name: Coonhound
intro: Coming all the way from the United States, is the Coonhound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. This is an American type of hunting dog developed for the hunting of raccoons and also for feral pigs, bobcats, cougars, and bears. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Cordoba Fighting Dog
intro: Straight from Argentina, meet the Cordoba Fighting Dog.
story: This is a guardian in a heavy frame, bred to hold ground and look like they mean it. The Córdoba fighting dog was a type of dog indigenous to Córdoba, Argentina, that resulted from crossbreeding old mastiff types of unknown pedigree. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Coton de Tulear
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Coton de Tulear.
story: From Madagascar, the Coton’s cottony white coat was a companion to merchants and royals in Toliara. They are cheerful, people-glued, and not a backyard-alone breed.

name: Cretan Hound
intro: Coming all the way from Crete, is the Cretan Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. This is a hunting dog from the Greek island of Crete. They are recognized both in Greece and in Germany. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Croatian Sheepdog
intro: Say hello to the Croatian Sheepdog, a Croatia original.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. They are one of seven recognised breeds of dog in Croatia, and one of two sheepdogs – the other is the Tornjak. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Curly Coated Retriever
intro: Rolling in from the United Kingdom: the Curly Coated Retriever.
story: One of the oldest retriever types, they wear a crisp curl that sheds water. Less famous than Labs, they are still serious gundogs with an independent streak.

name: Cursinu
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Cursinu.
story: Work and weather in their homeland shaped what you see in the breed today. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Cão de gado transmontano
intro: A Portuguese classic takes the stage: the Cão de gado transmontano.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. They originate in the historical province of Trás-os-Montes e Alto Douro in north-eastern Portugal, and is a rare breed confined mostly to this area. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Dandie Dinmont Terrier
intro: Fresh from Scotland, today’s daily dog is the Dandie Dinmont Terrier.
story: This is a vermin specialist at heart, bold for its size and not easily impressed. A Dandie Dinmont Terrier is a small Scottish dog breed in the terrier family. The breed has a very long body, short legs, and a distinctive topknot of hair on the head. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Danish Spitz
intro: Coming all the way from Denmark, is the Danish Spitz.
story: Prick ears, a curled tail, and a weatherproof coat: classic northern dog, even far from snow. This is a dog, originating from Denmark. The breed is known for making a good family pet, particularly as they are patient with children. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Danish Swedish Farmdog
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Danish Swedish Farmdog.
story: Scandinavia’s small farm all-rounder, once the Danish Pinscher. They ratted, herded, and announced the gate — a busy little worker, not a lap ornament.

name: Deutsche Bracke
intro: And today we have the Deutsche Bracke.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They are of the scenthound type, used for hunting both large and small game. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Dobermann
intro: Please welcome, from Germany, the Dobermann.
story: Louis Dobermann wanted a tax collector’s bodyguard in 19th-century Germany, and the sleek, athletic Dobermann was the result. They are sharp, loyal, and still look like they have an appointment.

name: Dogo Argentino
intro: Straight from Argentina, meet the Dogo Argentino.
story: Packed in Argentina as a big-game hunting mastiff, they are white, powerful, and bred to work in a pack. They need a handler who understands a serious hunting dog, not a fashion statement.

name: Dogo Sardesco
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Dogo Sardesco.
story: A further six are in the process of recognition by the ENCI. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Dogue Brasileiro
intro: From Brazil with a wag, here comes the Dogue Brasileiro.
story: This is a guardian in a heavy frame, bred to hold ground and look like they mean it. This is a mastiff-type working dog breed originating in Brazil. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Dogue de Bordeaux
intro: Say hello to the Dogue de Bordeaux, a French original.
story: A French mastiff with a massive head and a melting expression, they were baiting and guardian dogs before they were movie extras. They drool, they lean, and they take their people very seriously.

name: Double-nosed Andean tiger hound
intro: Coming all the way from the Andes, is the Double-nosed Andean tiger hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. The domestic dog was introduced to South America between 5,500 and 2,500 BCE from North America. They occupied the Andes region and spread into the Amazonian Basin relatively recently, in the 20th century.

name: Drentse Patrijshond
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Drentse Patrijshond.
story: Flushing and fetching birds shaped this dog — close-working, busy, and happiest in the field. This is a versatile spaniel-type hunting dog from the Dutch province of Drenthe. Called the Dutch Partridge Dog in English, approximately 5,000 dogs are registered with the breed club in the Netherlands, and breed clubs operate in Belgium, Denmark, Scandinavia and North America.

name: Drever
intro: A Swedish classic takes the stage: the Drever.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They are descended from the Westphalian Dachsbracke, a type of German hound called Bracke. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Dumfriesshire Hound
intro: Coming all the way from Scotland, is the Dumfriesshire Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. Dumfriesshire Black and Tan Foxhounds were a pack of foxhounds kennelled at Glenholm Kennels, Kettleholm, near Lockerbie until they were disbanded in 2001. They were established by Sir John Buchanan Jardine, author of Hounds of the World (1937), after the First World War.

name: Dunker
intro: Coming all the way from Norway, is the Dunker.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They were bred by Wilhelm Dunker to be a scenthound by crossing a Russian Harlequin Hound with dependable Norwegian scent hounds. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Dutch Shepherd
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Dutch Shepherd.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. They were used by shepherds and farmers who needed a versatile dog that made few demands and was able to adapt to a harsh and meager existence. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Dutch Smoushond
intro: And today we have the Dutch Smoushond.
story: They are related to the Pinscher and Schnauzer breed type formerly kept in stables to eliminate rats and mice. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Dutch Tulip Dog
intro: Please welcome, from the Netherlands, the Dutch Tulip Dog.
story: A Markiesje, also known as Dutch Tulip Dog, is believed to be an old dog breed. On several paintings dating from the 17th and 18th century a small, black dog resembling a Markiesje can be seen. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: East Siberian Laika
intro: Straight from Russia, meet the East Siberian Laika.
story: Cold miles and heavy loads wrote this breed: endurance first, sofa second. This is a Russian laika of spitz type, a hunting dog originating in parts of Siberia east of the Yenisei River. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: East-European Shepherd
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the East-European Shepherd.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. They were selectively bred in the Soviet Union from the German Shepherd to create a larger dog with better resistance to cold conditions, and was intended for military and guard work. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Ecuadorian Hairless Dog
intro: From Ecuador with a wag, here comes the Ecuadorian Hairless Dog.
story: The missing coat is the headline, but the breed is still a real dog underneath — watchful and warm-seeking. A hairless dog is a dog with a genetic disposition for hairlessness and hair loss. There are two known types of genetic hairlessness, a dominant and a recessive type.

name: English Cocker Spaniel
intro: Coming all the way from England, is the English Cocker Spaniel.
story: The original cocker, built to flush woodcock from cover, they are merrier and longer-backed than the American show type. A busy spaniel nose, a soft mouth, and a need to be in on every walk.

name: English Foxhound
intro: Rolling in from England: the English Foxhound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They are one of the four foxhound breeds of dog. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: English Mastiff
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the English Mastiff.
story: Among the heaviest of dogs, the Mastiff is an ancient guardian type, calm when well bred and monumental on the couch. They were never meant to jog in July.

name: English Pointer
intro: An English classic takes the stage: the English Pointer.
story: The classic English pointing dog: find birds, freeze, wait. Muscle and nose, with a switch that flips from statue to sprint.

name: English Setter
intro: Fresh from England, today’s daily dog is the English Setter.
story: A speckled English bird dog, they range and point with a waving tail. Gentle in the house, endless in the field, and still happiest when the day smells like grouse.

name: English Shepherd
intro: Coming all the way from the United States, is the English Shepherd.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. The work they were bred for in United States still shows in the body and the brain. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: English Springer Spaniel
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the English Springer Spaniel.
story: Springers flush — “spring” — birds from cover, then fetch. The happy, driving spaniel brain never really clocks out, which is why a tired Springer is a pleasant Springer.

name: English Toy Terrier
intro: And today we have the English Toy Terrier.
story: This is a vermin specialist at heart, bold for its size and not easily impressed. The work they were bred for in England still shows in the body and the brain. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: English Water Spaniel
intro: Please welcome, from the United Kingdom, the English Water Spaniel.
story: Flushing and fetching birds shaped this dog — close-working, busy, and happiest in the field. This is a dog that has been extinct since the first part of the 20th century, with the last specimen seen in the 1930s. They were best known for its use in hunting waterfowl and for being able to dive as well as a duck.

name: Entlebucher Mountain Dog
intro: Straight from Switzerland, meet the Entlebucher Mountain Dog.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. The Entlebucher Sennenhund or Entlebucher Mountain Dog is a medium-sized herding dog, they are the smallest of the four regional breeds that constitute the Sennenhund dog type. The name Sennenhund refers to people called Senn, herders in the Swiss Alps.

name: Estonian Hound
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Estonian Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They were bred in 1947 when the Soviet Union's national economy ministry decided that every country in the Union must have its own breed. They are happiest when the day has a task in it, not just a food bowl.

name: Estrela Mountain Dog
intro: From Portugal with a wag, here comes the Estrela Mountain Dog.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. The work they were bred for in Portugal still shows in the body and the brain. They want a person, a purpose, and enough room to be themselves.

name: Eurasier
intro: Say hello to the Eurasier, a German original.
story: A German companion spitz from Chow, Wolfspitz, and Samoyed stock, they are calm, reserved with strangers, and devoted at home. A family dog with a northern coat, not a toy.

name: Fawn Brittany Basset
intro: Rolling in from France: the Fawn Brittany Basset.

name: Königsberger Paukenhund
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Königsberger Paukenhund.
story: They were the traditional kettle drum dog of the Prussian infantry based in the East Prussian capital of Königsberg. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Laekenois
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Laekenois.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. They are bred in four distinct varieties based on coat type and colour: the long-haired black Groenendael; the rough-haired fawn Laekenois; the short-haired fawn Malinois, and the long-haired fawn Tervueren.

name: Lagotto Romagnolo
intro: And today we have the Lagotto Romagnolo.
story: Italy’s truffle dog, a curly water retriever that now hunts fungi instead of ducks. They are busy, sniffy, and happiest when their nose is employed.

name: Lancashire Heeler
intro: Please welcome, from England, the Lancashire Heeler.
story: A small British cattle dog that nipped heels, a cousin to the Corgi idea. Short, smart, and still sure the household needs herding.

name: Landseer
intro: Coming all the way from Germany and Switzerland, is the Landseer.
story: This is a black-and-white descendent of the Newfoundland that is recognized as an independent breed in continental Europe. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Lapponian Herder
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Lapponian Herder.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. The work they were bred for in Finland still shows in the body and the brain. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Large Münsterländer
intro: From Germany with a wag, here comes the Large Münsterländer.
story: Flushing and fetching birds shaped this dog — close-working, busy, and happiest in the field. They originated in Westphalia and Lower Saxony, and is named for the Münsterland region of northern Westphalia. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Large Vendeen Griffon Basset
intro: Say hello to the Large Vendeen Griffon Basset, a French original.
story: Work and weather in their homeland shaped what you see in the breed today. They are happiest when the day has a task in it, not just a food bowl.

name: Leonberger
intro: Rolling in from Germany: the Leonberger.
story: A German estate dog with a lion’s mane, they were drafted as draft and water dogs as well as companions. Big, wet, and usually kind, they still need room and a cool climate.

name: Lhasa Apso
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Lhasa Apso.
story: Sentinel dogs of Tibet, they wore a floor-length coat and a sharp alarm bark. They were never just lap ornaments — they still screen the door.

name: Limer
intro: Coming all the way from Medieval Europe, is the Limer.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. A limer, or lymer, was a kind of dog, a scenthound, used on a leash in medieval times to find large game before they were hunted down by the pack. They were sometimes known as a lyam hound/dog or lime-hound, from the Middle English word lyam, meaning 'leash'.

name: Lithuanian Hound
intro: Fresh from Lithuania, today’s daily dog is the Lithuanian Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. This is a rare, medium-size hunting dog from Lithuania. They are the only dog breed originating from Lithuania and dates back to the medieval Grand Duchy of Lithuania. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Lupo Italiano
intro: Coming all the way from Italy, is the Lupo Italiano.
story: An Italian herding and working dog whose founder claimed wolf blood from a German Shepherd cross. Genetics are less sure; the dog is still a serious, wolfish-looking worker.

name: Löwchen
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Löwchen.
story: They were built to fetch from water and cover, with a soft mouth and an eager brain. They once had the dubious distinction, like the Portuguese Water Dog and the Havanese, of being the rarest dog in the world. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Magyar agár
intro: And today we have the Magyar agár.
story: Hungary’s short-coated sighthound, the Magyar Agár. Built to course hare across the plains — less coat than a greyhound look, same afterburners.

name: Majorca Shepherd Dog
intro: Please welcome, from Mallorca, the Majorca Shepherd Dog.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. They are used as a shepherd dog, or as a watchdog or guard dog for rural property. They are happiest when the day has a task in it, not just a food bowl.

name: Mallorcan ratter
intro: Straight from Mallorca, meet the Mallorcan ratter.
story: They hunt by sight: a flash of motion can still light the afterburners. The work they were bred for in Mallorca still shows in the body and the brain. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Manchester Terrier
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Manchester Terrier.
story: A sleek English ratter, black and tan, they were pit and barn dogs before they were elegant companions. They still have a terrier motor.

name: Maneto
intro: Coming all the way from Andalusia in Spain, is the Maneto.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They are derived from the medium-sized Andalusian Hound, and is used to hunt rabbits, partridge, quail, and for retrieving ducks from the water. They are happiest when the day has a task in it, not just a food bowl.

name: Mantiqueira Shepherd
intro: Say hello to the Mantiqueira Shepherd, a Brazilian original.
story: A Brazilian herding dog of the Mantiqueira hills, nicknamed Policialzinho. Medium, busy, and still a livestock dog first.

name: Medium-sized Anglo-French Hound
intro: Rolling in from France: the Medium-sized Anglo-French Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They are one of the Anglo-French hound breeds which were created by crossing French scenthounds with English foxhounds. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Miniature American Shepherd
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Miniature American Shepherd.
story: A smaller Aussie built for agility and ranch work in a compact package. The herding brain is full-size even when the dog is not.

name: Miniature Australian Shepherd
intro: Coming all the way from the United States, is the Miniature Australian Shepherd.
story: A compact herding dog from American Aussie lines, they kept the full-size brain in a smaller frame. Bright, biddable, and still sure the household needs managing.

name: Miniature Fox Terrier
intro: Fresh from Australia, today’s daily dog is the Miniature Fox Terrier.
story: This is a vermin specialist at heart, bold for its size and not easily impressed. They are known colloquially in its native Australia as the “Mini Foxie”. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: Miniature Pinscher
intro: Coming all the way from Germany, is the Miniature Pinscher.
story: Not a tiny Dobermann — an older German ratter with a hackney gait and a huge self-image. They are busy, brave, and loud about the mail.

name: Miniature Schnauzer
intro: Hello pups, today’s daily dog is the Miniature Schnauzer.
story: A farm ratter from Germany, scaled down from the Standard Schnauzer, with the beard and eyebrows intact. They are busy terrier-cousins who still believe mice (and delivery trucks) need managing.

name: Mioritic
intro: And today we have the Mioritic.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. The work they were bred for in Romania still shows in the body and the brain. They still make the most sense with a job, even if today’s job is a long walk and a person who likes mud.

name: Molossus of Epirus
intro: Please welcome, from Greece, the Molossus of Epirus.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. Thought to be ancient in origin, the Greek Shepherd is very closely related to livestock guardian dog breeds from neighbouring countries; some dogs are believed to be simultaneously claimed to be other breeds as they migrate annually across national borders with the flocks they protect in search of seasonal pastures.

name: Montenegrin Mountain Hound
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Montenegrin Mountain Hound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. This is a rare dog breed originating from the mountainous regions of Montenegro. Black and tan, with a smooth coat, the Montenegrin Mountain Hound was called Black Hound in the past.

name: Morkie
intro: From the United States with a wag, here comes the Morkie.
story: These are crossbreed dogs created deliberately by crossing two purebred dogs. They want a person, a purpose, and enough room to be themselves.

name: Moscow Watchdog
intro: Say hello to the Moscow Watchdog, a Soviet Union original.
story: These dogs grew up beside the flock, a living fence more than a pet. This is a guard dog developed in the former Soviet Union, now Russia. It descends from crosses between the St. A good home still looks a lot like a partnership, not a decoration on a rug.

name: Mudhol Hound
intro: Rolling in from India: the Mudhol Hound.
story: They hunt by sight: a flash of motion can still light the afterburners. This is a sighthound from India. They are happiest when the day has a task in it, not just a food bowl.

name: Mudi
intro: Pups, gather round — it’s the Mudi.
story: A Hungarian herding spitz, curly-coated and electric. They work cattle and sheep with a lot of noise and even more opinion.

name: Neapolitan Mastiff
intro: From Ancient Rome, here comes the Neapolitan Mastiff.
story: The loose skin and massive head come from Italian guardian mastiffs meant to look like a nightmare at the gate. They are slow, devoted, and not built for heat or hurry.

name: Nenets Herding Laika
intro: Coming all the way from Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, is the Nenets Herding Laika.
story: Cold miles and heavy loads wrote this breed: endurance first, sofa second. Unlike other laikas, Nenets Herding Laika are less commonly used for hunting. A bored one will invent work — usually involving your shoes, the yard, or both.

name: New Guinea singing dog
intro: Coming all the way from New Guinea Highlands, is the New Guinea singing dog.
story: Also called New Guinea Highland dog is an ancient (basal) lineage of dog found in the New Guinea Highlands, on the island of New Guinea. Once considered to be a separate species in its own right, under the name Canis hallstromi, they are closely related to the Australian dingo.

name: Norfolk Terrier
intro: And today we have the Norfolk Terrier.
story: Drop-eared English farm terriers, small enough for a pocket and bold enough for a barn. They hunt, dig, and still believe they are large.

name: Norrbottenspets
intro: Please welcome, from Sweden, the Norrbottenspets.
story: A small Swedish hunting spitz, they found birds and squirrels in the northern woods. Prick ears, curled tail, and a weatherproof coat — still a hunter, not a sofa ornament.

name: Northern Inuit Dog
intro: Straight from England, meet the Northern Inuit Dog.
story: Cold miles and heavy loads wrote this breed: endurance first, sofa second. Tamaskan dogs are a dog breed from Finland that have been selectively bred to resemble a wolf or wolfdog. Although their exact origins are uncertain, these mixed breed dogs were primarily arctic breed crosses of Alaskan husky, Alaskan Malamute, Canadian Eskimo dog, German shepherd, Labrador husky, and Siberian husky.

name: Norwegian Buhund
intro: Today’s guest of honor: the Norwegian Buhund.
story: They were bred to move livestock with brain and stamina, not brute force. They are closely related to the Icelandic Sheepdog and the Jämthund. Leave them idle and you will meet the working breed the hard way.

name: Norwegian Elkhound
intro: From Norway with a wag, here comes the Norwegian Elkhound.
story: A nose like this was the whole point — they follow a trail the way other dogs follow a ball. They are one of the Northern Spitz-type breeds of dog and is the National Dog of Norway. The Elkhound has served as a hunter, guardian, herder, and defender. House life suits them when they get to use the body and brain they were built with.

name: Norwich Terrier
intro: Say hello to the Norwich Terrier, an English original.
story: The prick-eared twin to the Norfolk, another East Anglian ratter. Same engine, different ear set, same inability to mind their own business.

name: Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever
intro: Rolling in from Canada: the Nova Scotia Duck Tolling Retriever.
story: Tollers lure curious waterfowl into range with a foxlike dance, then retrieve the birds. From Nova Scotia, they are the smallest retriever — bright, busy, and vocal when the hunt is on.
